football_evidence.question: Can Memphis’ pass rush get to Kadin Semonza?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Tulane, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.5 of the 2.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Tulane has the ball (big plays on the ground): Tulane’s offense turns 10.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Memphis’ defense gives up explosive gains on 10.2% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.6%).
When Tulane has the ball (the run game against the run defense): Tulane’s offense averages 6.3 yards per carry, and Memphis’ defense allows 6.0 yards per carry (FBS average 5.1).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Tulane’s run defense No. 77 nationally and Memphis’ No. 128.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Tulane’s defense No. 73 nationally and Memphis’ No. 114.
contradicting: When Tulane has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Tulane’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.9% of its dropbacks, and Memphis’ defense sacks the quarterback on 8.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).

When Memphis has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Memphis’ offense has allowed a sack on 5.0% of its dropbacks, and Tulane’s defense sacks the quarterback on 3.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When Memphis has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Memphis’ offense averages 11.2 yards per pass attempt, and Tulane’s defense allows 7.6 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.5).
When Memphis has the ball (third down): Memphis’ offense converts 48.4% of its third downs, and Tulane’s defense allows opponents to convert 47.4% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).
quarterbacks: Kadin Semonza has completed 64 of 119 passes (53.8%) for 808 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in five games for Tulane, and has been sacked on 13 of 132 dropbacks.
Marcus Stokes has completed 101 of 144 passes (70.1%) for 1,543 yards, 10.7 yards per attempt, 17 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Memphis, and has been sacked on 8 of 152 dropbacks.

model: Tulane’s offense has to keep winning in the pass-rush matchup: it has allowed a sack on 8.9% of its dropbacks, and Memphis’ defense sacks the quarterback on 8.6% of opponent dropbacks.
Tulane’s defense has to slow Memphis on big pass plays — Memphis’ offense turns 16.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains.
Tulane’s offense has to keep winning on long runs: it turns 10.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Memphis’ defense gives up explosive gains on 10.2% of opponent runs.
Tulane’s offense has to keep winning on the ground: it averages 6.3 yards per carry, and Memphis’ defense allows 6.0 yards per carry.
